linkedin.text:
Restaurants ran $61.8 billion through Toast in three months.
Toast took in $1.62 billion from payments.

That's from Toast's Q3 report, out yesterday.

About 189,000 locations use Toast.
$1.24 billion of that $1.62 billion went to card-issuing banks, card networks and other costs.
$380 million was left for Toast.
The restaurant pays the whole stack either way.

Toast's net income: $169 million, up from $105 million a year ago.

Fair is fair: Toast builds good software, and restaurants pick it for a reason.

But here's what I can't get past.

Every one of those payments was a meal someone cooked, served and cleaned up after.
And a slice of every ticket went to fees: about $2.62 of every $100.

Do the math on your own shop.
On $500,000 a year in card sales, a 2.6% all-in rate is $13,000.
That's a cook's raise. A new fryer. A year of marketing.

As a nurse, I learned to watch the numbers nobody else checks.
Fees are one of those numbers.

Full disclosure: I started SVPay so shops can take payments without that fee.

Restaurant owners: divide last month's total fees by total card sales, then multiply by 100.
What all-in rate did you get?

#SmallBusiness #Restaurants #Payments
